clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female with a history of infertility, having undergone ovulation induction and IUI, presented to the ED with gradually worsening right lower quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness, and vomiting, following intercourse. An outpatient ultrasound showed a gestational sac in the uterus, a cystic mass in the right adnexa, and fluid in the pelvis, raising concern for heterotopic pregnancy. Initial vital signs included tachycardia (HR 109 bpm), and physical exam revealed right lower quadrant tenderness. There was a significant increase in abdominal bleeding noted between a POCUS and the outpatient ultrasound. Exploratory laparoscopy confirmed the diagnosis, revealing a dilated right fallopian tube due to ectopic pregnancy and a 1cm paratubal cyst. A right salpingectomy was performed, and 100mL of intra-abdominal blood was evacuated. The patient was discharged the next day. Four weeks later, the intrauterine pregnancy, then at 6 weeks 6 days gestation, was terminated via dilation and curettage.
